about: Stage 8 vectors. Each case: a signed key list, a proof, the pinned identity fingerprint, an optional required authority id, and the verdict or refusal the Rust reference gives. Regenerated and compared by tools/nanorix-verify/tests/trust_chain_vectors.rs.

cases.name: active_version_resolves
cases.note: The pinned identity signed the list; the proof's authority and key version are in it. Stage 8.

cases.name: required_authority_matches
cases.note: As above, with a required authority id equal to the proof's.

cases.name: archived_version_resolves
cases.note: The proof's key version was archived by a rotation; the list still holds it, so it resolves.

cases.name: rotated_active_version_resolves
cases.note: After the rotation, a proof under the new active version resolves.

cases.name: wrong_pin_refused
cases.note: The pin names another identity than the one that signed the list. Refused before any proof is checked.

cases.name: list_signed_by_other_identity_refused
cases.note: A well-formed list signed by, and naming, another identity, checked under the customer's pin.

cases.name: list_claiming_pinned_fingerprint_with_other_key_refused
cases.note: Another identity's list whose fingerprint field is relabelled to the pin; the inline key still hashes to the other identity.

cases.name: list_claiming_pinned_identity_fully_refused
cases.note: Another identity's list relabelled with the pinned fingerprint and the pinned public key; only the signature is not the pinned identity's.

cases.name: authority_key_edited_after_signing_refused
cases.note: An authority's public key was replaced after the list was signed.

cases.name: archived_row_removed_after_signing_refused
cases.note: The archived row was deleted after signing; a proof under it would otherwise be lost.

cases.name: non_strict_only_signature_refused
cases.note: A small-order identity key and a signature that a non-strict Ed25519 check accepts for any message. The pin is that key's own fingerprint.

cases.name: key_version_not_in_list
cases.note: The proof names version 2; the list holds only version 1. Stage 6.

cases.name: authority_not_in_list
cases.note: A proof naming Nanorix's default authority, checked against the customer's list. The list does not hold that authority. Stage 6.

cases.name: required_authority_mismatch
cases.note: The customer's proof under a required authority id naming Nanorix's default authority. Refused at stage 2 by the policy pin, before the list is read.

cases.name: required_authority_absent_from_proof
cases.note: A proof with no authority_id under a required authority id other than the default.

cases.name: different_key_under_listed_version
cases.note: The proof's embedded key verifies its own signature but is not the key the list holds under that version. Stage 7.

cases.name: absent_authority_field_means_default
cases.note: A proof with no authority_id is read as Nanorix's default authority and resolved in a list that holds it.

cases.name: default_authority_in_list_resolves
cases.note: Both authorities in one signed list; the proof under Nanorix's default authority resolves to its own key.

cases.name: revoked_authority
cases.note: The list marks the authority revoked. Stage 8 is reached and the proof is not valid.

cases.name: active_row_wins_over_archived_row
cases.note: One version name in both lists with different keys. A proof signed by the active key resolves.

cases.name: archived_row_never_used_when_active_has_name
cases.note: Same list; a proof signed by the archived row's key is checked against the active key. Stage 7.

cases.name: defaults_omitted_in_published_list
cases.note: The published list leaves out archived_versions and revoked; the signature was made over the list with both filled in.

cases.name: unknown_fields_are_not_covered
cases.note: Fields the reference does not read were added after signing. The reference ignores them and the list verifies.

cases.name: pqc_slot_is_not_covered
cases.note: The reserved post-quantum signature slot is populated with a value. It is outside the signed bytes.

cases.name: signature_without_base64_prefix
cases.note: The manifest signature is given without its base64: prefix.

cases.name: list_missing_required_field
cases.note: An authority record without display_name does not parse as a key list.

cases.name: key_record_algorithm_is_signed
cases.note: The key record carries algorithm, as every hosted key record does. It is in the signed bytes.

cases.name: algorithm_edited_after_signing_refused
cases.note: The key record's algorithm was changed after signing.

cases.name: algorithm_not_a_string
cases.note: A key record's algorithm that is not a string does not parse as a key list.

cases.name: marked_authority_resolves
cases.note: The list marks the authority as emitting population heads. The marker is in the signed bytes.

cases.name: marker_removed_after_signing_refused
cases.note: The marker was removed after signing, which would hide that the authority emits heads.

cases.name: marker_added_after_signing_refused
cases.note: The marker was added to a list signed without it.

cases.name: marker_false_signs_as_absent
cases.note: A marker of false is not in the signed bytes, the same as no marker.

cases.name: marker_not_boolean
cases.note: A marker that is not a boolean does not parse as a key list.

cases.name: identity_key_empty
cases.note: A list that carries no identity public key cannot be checked against a pin.

cases.name: utf8_bom_refused
cases.note: customer_v1 with a UTF-8 byte order mark in front. serde_json refuses it; a parser that skips the mark would load the list.

cases.name: utf16_refused
cases.note: customer_v1 written as UTF-16 with its byte order mark. The reference reads UTF-8 only.

cases.name: utf32_refused
cases.note: customer_v1 written as UTF-32 with its byte order mark. The reference reads UTF-8 only.

cases.name: nan_refused
cases.note: customer_v1 with one member the reference does not read, whose value is NaN, which is not JSON.

cases.name: customer_only_corpus_proof_resolves
cases.note: The corpus's signed customer_only proof (13_customer_only/0000), whose signed labels name the customer authority, resolves in the key list published for that authority under that list's own pin. Stage 8, the same as nanorix_only.

cases.name: v1_0_proof_never_anchors
cases.note: A genuine 1.0 proof whose final_hash is signed by the key the list holds for Nanorix's default authority under version 1, checked against that list under its pin. A 1.0 signature covers final_hash alone, which binds destroyed_at and the two optional Merkle roots. It does not bind the capsule_id itself (only through record receipts, which a holder can remove), the region or the key id, so a 1.0 proof is never anchored: stage 7, not stage 8. The proof's capsule_started event names a region, which no verifier may report.

cases.name: v1_0_revoked_authority
cases.note: The same 1.0 proof under a list that marks Nanorix's default authority revoked. A 1.0 proof runs the revocation check as 2.x does, so it is refused at stage 8 like a 2.x proof.

cases.name: v1_0_forgery_under_list
cases.note: A 1.0 proof self-signed with a key of its own, naming version 1 of Nanorix's default authority. Its signature verifies on the key it carries and not on the listed key, so it is refused at stage 7, as a 2.x forgery is.

cases.name: infinity_refused
cases.note: customer_v1 with one member the reference does not read, whose value is -Infinity, which is not JSON.
